**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.8. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

When a high-dimensional observation must be compressed, we project it into a smaller subspace. The closest point in an orthogonal projection minimises Euclidean reconstruction error.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\operatorname{proj}_{\boldsymbol u}(\boldsymbol x)=\frac{\boldsymbol u^\top\boldsymbol x}{\boldsymbol u^\top\boldsymbol u}\boldsymbol u
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

Project x=(3,1) onto u=(1,1): the coefficient is (3+1)/(1+1)=2, yielding (2,2). The residual (1,-1) is orthogonal to u; its dot product with (1,1) is zero.

## What follows, and what does not

Projection connects least-squares regression and PCA. If Q has orthonormal columns, the projection into its span is QQ^T x.

## Test your reasoning

Project (2,3) onto the x-axis, then compute the squared reconstruction error.
